description: SS-31 (elamipretide) is a mitochondria-targeted tetrapeptide containing D-arginine and 2′,6′-dimethyltyrosine. Its design gives it affinity for cardiolipin on the inner mitochondrial membrane, and it is one of the most-cited tool peptides in mitochondrial-dysfunction and bioenergetics research, where it is used to probe electron-transport-chain efficiency and reactive-oxygen-species endpoints in cell and animal models.

faq.question: What is SS-31?
faq.answer: SS-31 (elamipretide) is a mitochondria-targeted tetrapeptide, CAS 736992-21-5, used as a research reagent in mitochondrial-biology studies.

faq.question: Why does SS-31 contain D-amino acids?
faq.answer: The D-arginine and dimethyltyrosine residues improve metabolic stability and give the peptide its cardiolipin-binding character, which is why it is used as a targeted mitochondrial tool rather than a signalling peptide.

faq.question: How does SS-31 differ from MOTS-c?
faq.answer: Both are studied in mitochondrial research, but MOTS-c is a mitochondrial-DNA-encoded 16-residue peptide studied for metabolic signalling, while SS-31 is a synthetic, cell-penetrating tetrapeptide that binds cardiolipin.
